method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a city that has hosted the modern Olympics.
questions.scope: Summer and Winter hosts count; ancient host cities alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name a branch or field of mathematics.
questions.scope: Recognized mathematical branches, subfields and established mathematical research disciplines count. Both pure and applied mathematics count. Individual formulas, symbols, isolated theorems and unrelated school subjects do not by themselves name a branch.

questions.prompt: Name a type of knife.
questions.scope: Real knife styles and knife-like edged hand tools count, including kitchen, craft, hunting and surgical knives. Medical devices that only use knife metaphorically do not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has been on the San Francisco 49ers franchise roster.
questions.scope: Past or present roster membership for this franchise through the retained 2026 snapshot counts, including its earlier names/locations and NFL, AFL or AAFC membership where applicable. Offseason and practice squads count. An unrelated former team sharing the same city or code does not. The current franchise rules and captured seasons are retained for source review.

questions.prompt: Name a playable Legend from Apex Legends.
questions.scope: Released playable Apex Legends characters count. NPCs and unreleased datamined characters do not.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a real island or archipelago.
questions.scope: Real named islands and archipelagos worldwide count, including islands that share a country name. Continental mainlands are not treated as islands. Fictional islands do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a plant people eat.
questions.scope: Named edible plants count, including those eaten for fruit, leaves, roots or seeds; fungi are separate.

questions.prompt: Name a track on J. Cole’s Born Sinner.
questions.scope: The complete standard album and the five deluxe bonus tracks (also called Truly Yours 3) count, including named skits and interludes. Other albums and the separate Truly Yours and Truly Yours 2 EPs do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a knot, bend, hitch or splice.
questions.scope: Named, established examples of the whole everyday subject count. Public brand names and actual alternative names share one answer. Generic descriptions or invented combinations do not create new identities.

questions.prompt: Name a type of chili or bell pepper.
questions.scope: Real named Capsicum pepper kinds/cultivars and documented dried names count. Fresh/dried names of one pepper share identity where they identify the same pepper. Black pepper and arbitrary color-plus-food labels are not Capsicum types.

questions.prompt: Name something that produces visible light.
questions.scope: Natural sources and human-made devices count; a reflector alone does not.

questions.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
questions.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a car, motorcycle, truck or bus manufacturer or brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical manufacturers and established marques of cars, motorcycles (including racing motorcycles), trucks and buses count, including documented vehicle assembly and coachbuilding firms. A vehicle model alone, a transport operator, an aircraft/rail-only maker, a pure component supplier, a toy or a fictional brand does not count. Actual brand/company names and true renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name a type of domestic animal.
Name a fictional robot.
questions.scope: Robots and droids from films, TV, books or games count; actors and real-world robots do not.

questions.prompt: Name something people open using a key or a code.
questions.scope: Physical objects and devices count; the code can be a password or combination.

questions.prompt: Name a real ice-cream flavor.
questions.scope: Established ice-cream and gelato flavor names, including named branded flavors and dairy-free ice-cream equivalents, count. An invented combination is not automatically an established flavor. A sorbet-only flavor is not evidence of an ice-cream flavor.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a video game console or dedicated gaming handheld.
questions.scope: Named released game consoles, dedicated handheld game systems and purpose-built gaming handheld PCs count. Named revisions, early electronic/VHS-based gaming systems and game-library add-on platforms count; regional renames of the same platform share an answer. N-Gage is a documented gaming-handheld hybrid. General-purpose phones/computers, media-streaming boxes with optional games, unreleased prototypes and input-only controllers do not count. A self-contained plug-and-play game unit counts even if its shell resembles a controller.

questions.prompt: Name a spy or secret agent from fiction.
questions.scope: Named fictional intelligence agents, spies, spymasters and documented clandestine/covert operatives from any medium count, including covert support agents and private fictional agencies. A secret identity, ordinary detective/police work, a group/show title, performer or an unnamed generic agent is not automatically a spy. Actual aliases share identity; different characters, clones and officeholders are not merged merely because they share a codename.

questions.prompt: Name a volcano or named volcanic complex. Dormant and extinct ones count.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of personal protective equipment.
questions.scope: Recognized personal protective equipment and its named types count, including head, face, hearing, hand, foot, respiratory, fall, flotation and protective-clothing equipment. This classifies equipment names, not suitability for a particular hazard. Ordinary office tools, hand sanitizer and everyday clothing without a protective function do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a percussion instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a carnivorous plant.
questions.scope: Documented carnivorous plants and recognized named groups count. A whole mixed genus must not bring in non-carnivorous species. Fictional man-eating plants do not count. Cultivar epithets need their plant/genus qualification. Registered and independently documented cultivated forms count; a nomenclatural status alone does not decide real horticultural use.

questions.prompt: Name an edible leafy green.
questions.scope: Named examples of the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public synonyms share one answer; arbitrary initials and invented combinations do not.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Atlanta Hawks.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Earlier NBA seasons as the Tri-Cities Blackhawks, Milwaukee Hawks and St. Louis Hawks count.

questions.prompt: Name a science fiction movie.
Name a sporting-goods or outdoor-equipment retail chain.
questions.scope: Actual named places, institutions, companies or objects in the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public alternative names share one answer. Abbreviations must be actual published names, not generated initials.

questions.prompt: Name a weapon or grenade in Counter-Strike 2. Knife types count.
questions.scope: Base weapons, explosives and knife models count; cosmetic finishes, gloves and healing items do not.

questions.prompt: Name a color or a named shade.
questions.scope: Recognized English color names and published named shades count, including named pigments, Crayola colors and standard CSS color keywords. Regional spellings and ordinary synonyms share one answer. Patterns are not a single color. Different standard definitions of the same ordinary name do not create extra answers.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of mollusc.
questions.scope: Named mollusc groups and species count, including gastropods, bivalves, cephalopods, chitons and other mollusc lineages. Common and scientific names count. Crustaceans, echinoderms and cnidarians do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an ice-cream topping or mix-in.
questions.scope: Named toppings and mix-ins used on ice cream, gelato or frozen custard count, including candy, fruit, nuts, sauces and cake pieces. A flavor by itself is not a topping.

questions.prompt: Name a club that has won the Stanley Cup.
questions.scope: Documented champion clubs across the Stanley Cup’s history count, including pre-NHL champions. The original Ottawa Senators club is distinct from the modern expansion team. Historical names of the same continuous winning franchise score once.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Toy Story franchise.
questions.scope: Named or distinctly identified characters from Toy Story films, shorts, series and the Lightyear spin-off count. Established collective character identities such as the Aliens count. Voice actors, film titles and descriptive organizational headings do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a holiday, traditional festival or recognized observance.
questions.scope: Real named religious/civic holidays, traditional festivals and established calendar observances count, including historical or regional observances and named periods such as Advent or Ramadan. Modern stand-alone concert/film festivals and conferences are a different subject. A calendar date, month, weekday, person, deity, place, ritual or campaign theme is not automatically an observance. Shared dates and related ancestry do not merge distinct observances; substitute dates do not create new ones.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Green Day.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Green Day count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a type of electromagnetic or particle radiation, or a named spectrum band.
questions.scope: Electromagnetic or particle-radiation types, real named emission processes, physical-origin categories and recognized spectrum bands count. This includes established theoretical predictions such as Hawking radiation; naming a type does not claim it has been directly observed. Acoustic waves, ocean waves, static fields, gravitational waves and fictional energy are outside this electromagnetic/particle scope.

questions.prompt: Name a type of room or specialized indoor space.
Name a game on Steam tagged “Action”.
Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a cooking or food-preparation technique.
questions.scope: Recognized techniques for cooking, preparing, cutting, mixing, baking or preserving food count. Real public verb/noun forms share an answer. An ingredient, utensil, finished dish or desired texture alone is not a technique.

questions.prompt: Name a real named concert venue, opera house or music arena.
questions.scope: Named examples of the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public synonyms share one answer; arbitrary initials and invented combinations do not.

questions.prompt: Name a human organ.
questions.scope: Recognized scientific names and established public synonyms for the whole subject count. Different spellings of one identity score once. Unrelated everyday meanings and invented initials do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a fairy tale or traditional folk tale.
questions.scope: Recognized named traditional folk tales and published literary fairy tales count, including documented fairy-tale novels. Actual translated/alternate titles of a tale share an answer. Whole anthologies, authors and arbitrary modern fantasy novels do not automatically qualify. Different tales are not merged merely because they have a shared ATU plot number or point to a shared character/collection article.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a song with a color in its title.
questions.scope: Ordinary color words in released song titles count; color names used as surnames need context.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has won the AP NFL regular-season MVP award.
questions.scope: Winners of the Associated Press NFL regular-season MVP award from 1957 onward count. Super Bowl MVP and other organizations’ MVP awards alone do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that digs or lives in a burrow.
questions.scope: Recognized common names, scientific names and established named kinds count. A documented natural example is required; invented combinations and individual pet names do not.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Dota 2.
questions.scope: The complete official playable hero roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts. Items, cosmetics and non-playable creeps are not heroes.

questions.prompt: Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name a song by Childish Gambino.
questions.scope: Released song titles with the named artist as a lead or vocal guest count, including released mixtape songs and actual group performances. Production-only credits, unofficial leaks and instrumental-only versions do not count. Clean/explicit, live and remix variants share an identity.

questions.prompt: Name an online social or community platform.
questions.scope: Real current or historical general-audience social networks, social media and named online community platforms count, including group communication, public discussion networks and social virtual worlds. Ordinary email, devices, generic internet terms, individual profiles/groups, learning-management software and services dedicated to dating or adult content do not. Actual public names such as X, VK, QQ and Hi5 count; generated initials do not.

questions.prompt: Name an ice-cream or frozen-dessert brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical ice-cream, gelato, frozen-custard, frozen-yogurt, sorbet, ice-pop and branded ice/slush treats count. Documented specialty chains, actual licensed product-line brands and store labels count. Different flavors, package sizes and unbranded desserts are not brands; neither pet food nor a company with no proven frozen-dessert product qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a character from Madagascar.
questions.scope: Named characters appearing in the original franchise, its direct adaptations or sequels count. Actors, production staff, fan characters and characters appearing only in unrelated crossover games do not. Public aliases of one character share a scoring identity.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of moth.
questions.scope: Recognized kinds, named groups and species count, including documented extinct examples. Common and scientific synonyms share one identity. Age, sex, individual pet names and invented color combinations do not count as kinds.

questions.prompt: Name a board or card game people can play together offline.
questions.scope: Published games and traditional named games count; video games do not.

questions.prompt: Name a category of motor vehicle.
questions.scope: Types of self-propelled road or off-road vehicle count, with wheels, tracks or skids, including electric versions. Individual named models, rail vehicles, unpowered trailers and descriptions of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Lana Del Rey.
questions.scope: Released song titles with Lana Del Rey as a lead or vocal guest count, including released mixtape songs and actual group performances. Production-only credits, unofficial leaks and instrumental-only versions do not count. Clean/explicit, live and remix variants share an answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a type of flooring or floor covering.
questions.scope: Named examples of the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public synonyms share one answer; arbitrary initials and invented combinations do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of mechanical engine or motor.
questions.scope: Recognized mechanical prime movers and engine or motor types count, including combustion engines, turbines, rocket engines and electric, hydraulic or pneumatic motors. Electric generators, software engines and whole vehicles do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a type or form of poem.
questions.scope: Recognized named poem and verse forms count, including complete short forms and established stanza/verse forms used as poems. A subject, individual poet, book title or meter alone does not automatically name a poem form.

questions.prompt: Name an athlete featured on a video game's cover or in its title.
questions.scope: An officially released sports game's cover athlete or title namesake qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a named salad or established salad variety.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a named character from Undertale or Deltarune.
questions.scope: Officially released named examples from the stated game or franchise count. Mods, fan creations, unreleased leaks, unrelated crossovers and production staff do not. Alternate public names share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of woodpecker.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Picidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an object designed to be inflated.
questions.scope: Common inflatable objects and named inflatable equipment types count, whether filled with air, helium or another gas. Objects merely containing an empty cavity do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a hotel chain or hotel brand.
questions.scope: Real current or historical hotel, motel, hostel and serviced-apartment brands/chains, branded hotel collections and primarily hotel-operating groups count. Single independent properties, booking/rental marketplaces, private-equity investors and unrelated parent companies do not. Genuine short names and brand renames share an answer.

questions.prompt: Name a record label or record company.
questions.scope: Real current and historical record labels, imprints and record companies count. A publisher, streaming platform or music store is not automatically a record label.

questions.prompt: Name a heist movie.
questions.scope: Films built around a robbery, theft, con or organized caper count, including comedies, animated movies and shorts. Television series, directors and a film with only an unrelated passing theft do not automatically count.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a Pokémon type.
questions.scope: The 18 standard main-series types and the special Stellar Tera type count. The unused Bird/??? data labels and the spin-off Shadow classification are outside this explicitly main-series type list.

questions.prompt: Name a type of flower.
questions.scope: Recognized common flower types and flowering plants grown for their blooms count, including named horticultural groups and documented varieties. Materials merely named after flowers, artificial flower products and unrelated decorative objects do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a named type of bread.
questions.scope: Named breads, rolls and flatbreads count; filling-only variations do not create a new bread.

questions.prompt: Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name a guitar manufacturer or established guitar brand, including historical makers.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a comedy movie.
Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or recognized sporting discipline played on snow or ice.
questions.scope: Established ice and snow sports and competitive disciplines count. A sport merely played during the winter on an ordinary indoor court does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a video game you can play with someone on the same screen or console.
questions.scope: Local co-op, split-screen and shared-screen multiplayer count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a recognized phobia or named fear.
questions.scope: Established named fears, including well-documented colloquial phobia names, count. Not every term is an independent clinical diagnosis; prejudice labels and invented words do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Red Hot Chili Peppers.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Red Hot Chili Peppers count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a Japanese dish or established Japanese food.
questions.scope: Established named foods, products or varieties matching the whole subject count. Actual public synonyms share one identity. Invented ingredient combinations and generic descriptions do not create new answers.

questions.prompt: Name a crime TV or streaming show.
Name a type of staircase, ladder or step access.
questions.scope: Named examples of the whole subject count, including documented historical examples. Real public synonyms share one answer; arbitrary initials and invented combinations do not.

questions.prompt: Name a real named award, prize, medal or trophy.
questions.scope: Actual named awards, prizes, medals, orders and trophies across arts, sports, science and public life count, including historical awards and genuine named award families. Real named categories are answers within this one subject. A generic placing/medal, recipient, sponsor, organization, tournament, festival or hall-of-fame membership is not automatically a named award. Different awards sharing a public surname/title remain distinct and use qualifiers where needed.

questions.prompt: Name a character from a Sonic the Hedgehog game.
questions.scope: Named characters that appear in released Sonic video games count. Voice actors and characters appearing only in unrelated crossover franchises do not.

questions.prompt: Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a programming, scripting, query, markup or stylesheet language.
questions.scope: Real current and historical computer languages for programs, scripts, database queries, markup or style sheets count. Named dialects also count. Plain data-file formats, code editors and ordinary spoken languages do not count. Named XML vocabularies and document-markup formats count; an organization, generic data model, element or software platform alone is not a language.

questions.prompt: Name a wild animal in the dog family.
questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named animal groups, count. English names, documented scientific names and genuine public synonyms count. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory. Domestic dog breeds do not count. Dingoes and New Guinea singing dogs count as established wild-dog groups; their disputed species rank does not make their names invalid.

questions.prompt: Name a named character from Looney Tunes.
questions.scope: Named characters belonging to the main official franchise count, including named supporting and one-episode characters. Actors, production credits, fan creations and crossover-only guests do not qualify. Actual public nicknames and personas share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a tea brand or tea company.
questions.scope: Real current or historical tea brands, tea companies and tea estates count. A tea variety, drink preparation or generic ingredient is not a company or brand. The inventory includes packaged-tea and ready-to-drink brands; owning a separate brand does not automatically make a generic parent-name guess eligible.
